lines: Irregular, heavy menstrual bleeding and pelvic pressure for 6 months

She has never been pregnant and mentions that her menstrual cycles have been anovulatory for the past year.
She reports a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension.
Smoking: Current smoker, 1 pack per day.
Alcohol: Former social drinker (1 glass wine nightly), currently denies alcohol use.
Occupation: Office administrator and part-time retail associate.
She has a BMI of 35 kg/m^2
On physical examination, her abdomen is obese but non-tender, and a bimanual pelvic exam reveals an enlarged, smooth uterus without adnexal masses.

Her most recent Pap test showed atypical glandular cells.

encounters.cc: Fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion for 3 months

lines: Fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion for 3 months

The patient is a 52-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and dyslipidemia who returns to the Internal Medicine clinic three months following evaluation by Obstetrics and Gynecology for irregular heavy menstrual bleeding and pelvic pressure.
She presents to the clinic with a 3-month history of fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion.
She has a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Her medications include metformin and lisinopril.
Smoking: Current smoker, 1 pack per day.
Alcohol: Former social drinker (1 glass wine nightly), currently denies alcohol use.
Occupation: Office administrator and part-time retail associate.
She denies chest pain, palpitations, or lower extremity edema.
On physical examination, her blood pressure is 142/88 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and BMI is 32 kg/m^2.
Lung auscultation reveals no crackles or wheezes.

lines: Routine health check-up with concerns regarding Alzheimer's disease risk given maternal history

The patient has a history of hypertension, which is currently managed with lisinopril, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, controlled with metformin.
Her current medications include lisinopril 20 mg daily, metformin 500 mg twice daily, and atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Her mother was diagnosed with it at the age of 70.

Her physical examination is otherwise unremarkable.

encounters.cc: Intermittent pain and swelling in hands, wrists, and knees with morning stiffness

lines: Intermittent pain and swelling in hands, wrists, and knees with morning stiffness

The patient is a 53-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and dyslipidemia who presents with joint symptoms following recent encounters for complex atypical endometrial hyperplasia and iron deficiency anemia.
Over the past few years, she has experienced intermittent pain and swelling in her hands, wrists, and knees.
These symptoms tend to worsen in the mornings and improve slightly throughout the day.
She has had several similar flares in the past that lasted a few weeks and resolved with over-the-counter medications.
The patient reports increased fatigue and stiffness recently, especially in the mornings.
She works part-time as a librarian and has difficulty shelving books during flares.
Her past medical history includes type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension.
She is not on any disease-modifying medications.
Smokes one pack of cigarettes per day. She drinks one glass of wine nightly.
She has a BMI of 32.1 kg/m².
Temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure is 142/90 mmHg, pulse is 78/min, and respirations are 16/min.
Physical examination reveals tenderness and mild swelling in both wrists and the second and third metacarpophalangeal joints bilaterally.
Laboratory studies reveal a positive rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, with mild elevation in ESR and CRP.

encounters.cc: Progressive blurring of vision in both eyes over the past 6 months without pain

lines: Progressive blurring of vision in both eyes over the past 6 months without pain
This patient with diabetes and rheumatoid arthritis returns.
She reports no pain or redness in either eye.
Her diabetes has been poorly controlled.
Her current medications include metformin and lisinopril.
Smoking: Current smoker, 1 pack per day.
Alcohol: Former social drinker (1 glass wine nightly), currently denies alcohol use.
Occupation: Office administrator and part-time retail associate.
Her blood pressure is 140/85 mmHg, and her BMI is 32 kg/m^2.
On ophthalmologic examination, you note several microaneurysms, dot-blot hemorrhages, and hard exudates in the retina of both eyes.
There is also evidence of macular edema.

lines: Gradual increase in abdominal girth over the past year attributed to aging

encounters.cc: Acute worsening of fatigue, exertional dyspnea, and 15-pound unintentional weight loss over 6 months

lines: Acute worsening of fatigue, exertional dyspnea, and 15-pound unintentional weight loss over 6 months
This 56-year-old female with Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and a history of iron deficiency anemia presents with acute worsening of fatigue and exertional dyspnea.
She reports a 15-pound unintentional weight loss over the same period.
- Diabetic Macular Edema (Clinically Significant Macular Edema) secondary to Non-proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (diagnosed 2021-11-15)
She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension.
Her medications include metformin and lisinopril.
She works two jobs and has limited time for physical activity.
She admits to a diet high in processed foods because they are more affordable and accessible in her neighborhood.
On physical examination, her blood pressure is 142/90 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and BMI is 32 kg/m^2.
Lower extremity examination shows 1+ pitting edema.
- Urinalysis: 2+ protein, no glucose or ketones
Chest X-ray shows cardiomegaly and pulmonary congestion.
An echocardiogram demonstrates left ventricular hypertrophy with an ejection fraction of 40%.
